dedupe_keys.name: hp catch hydropower cascade and catchment analysis

description: HP-CatCH is Python code for constructing and analysing hydropower cascade networks across Switzerland and their contributing catchments. Yann Yasser Haddad and collaborators publish the repository alongside an Earth System Science Data discussion preprint from August 2026. The code loads plant registries, reservoirs, water intakes, pressure tunnels, catchment polygons and elevation data. It extracts directed cascade topology, traces upstream contributors and computes catchment-to-reservoir weights. Analysis functions aggregate inflows and examine water utilisation. Outputs include CSV node and flow tables and geospatial shapefiles, as described in the public documentation. The code is free under the MIT licence and available without registration. Python 3.11 or later and geospatial dependencies are required. External inputs are configured through file paths and are not included as a complete runnable example. The national companion dataset describes 48 cascades and 601 run-of-river plants, but its ETH landing page returned HTTP 429 during this check. Code inspection here was limited to documentation and metadata; execution and reproduced inflows were not tested. The preprint remains under review. This model could support water-energy dependency analysis and climate adaptation studies in Switzerland.
